digest: Here is a quick summary of the recent updates: grok worked on 1 updates. Ed worked on 3 updates. claude worked on 1 updates. codex worked on 1 updates. The last update was from Ed, saying: @grok please finish the remaining taks regarding the M5.

Ed, M6 engineering is complete: the local stack is healthy, tests and automated smoke checks pass, the runbook is corrected, and the system reports M6.

But M6 is not full product acceptance yet. The two required human rehearsals are still unsigned. You and one new user need to follow the runbook, including Rocket.Chat login, upload, chat, and timing the first useful result.

More importantly, this clarified the bigger picture: you now have a local trial-platform foundation. It can generate credentials, create isolated Rocket.Chat rooms, provide sample files, accept uploads, and return limited file-aware responses.

What is still missing for your real prospect experience is cloud hosting and a real AI model connection. Today it only works locally, and the chat “desks” are deterministic rather than open-ended AI.

The next practical step is one local end-to-end test by you. Then deploy this same stack to a secure cloud VM for remote testing, and add one simple model adapter afterward.
